items.title: Howard Alden interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997
items.q: Red Holloway and Sweets Edison would be playing — they’re friends of mine, I play with them, we get along fine

ctx.x: Yeah, I see in the audience too, even more in the audience.

Well yeah. That’s definitely true. I’m not sure exactly why. It’s kind of a drag. Last time I did one of those jazz cruises a couple of years ago, again, like I’d be playing with Flip Phillips, Kenny Davern, Milt Hinton on bass — look out, the audience is all white pretty much. And look in the next room, Red Holloway and Sweets Edison would be playing — they’re friends of mine, I play with them, we get along fine — but the audience would be all black, for whatever reason. And I wish — the white people could gain…
You mentioned a couple of times, one of our favorite people at Hamilton and that’s Milt Hinton. He’s quite a treasure, as is Mona.
